captions: Hello, and welcome to Atomic English, Stage 3. In this lesson: Animal fact file.
Read a fact file and find information quickly.
Here are some new words. Habitat. The place where an animal lives. Mammal.
An animal with fur that feeds its babies milk. Insect. A small animal with six legs.
Listen and say them. habitat
mammal
insect.
And some more words. Wings. Parts of the body used for flying. Hunt.
Look for and catch animals to eat. Nest. A home that birds make. Listen and say them.
wings
hunt
nest.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: the place where an animal lives?
Now some grammar: Facts in the present simple.
Fact files use the present simple because facts are true all the time.
For example: Bees make honey. For example: An owl hunts at night.
Now listen, and read along. Fact file: The barn owl.
Type of animal: bird Habitat: farms,
fields and old buildings Food: mice and other small animals Size:
about 35 centimetres long Amazing fact: A barn owl hunts at night.
It can hear a mouse moving under the grass.
Its soft wings make almost no sound, so the mouse cannot hear it coming.
Another question. The video will stop. What type of animal is a barn owl?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like habitat, mammal, insect.
You practised facts in the present simple. And you read Fact file: The barn owl.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!

sections.title: Bigger and faster

q.prompt: What is the biggest animal in the world?
q.reason: The blue whale is the biggest animal.

options.fb: The blue whale is the biggest animal.

captions: Hello, and welcome to Atomic English, Stage 3. In this lesson: Bigger and faster.
Compare animals using comparatives.
Here are some new words. Heavy. Weighs a lot. Fast. Moves very quickly. Tiny.
Very, very small. Listen and say them. heavy
fast
tiny.
And some more words. Huge. Very, very big. Weigh. Find out how heavy something is.
Record. The best or most ever. Listen and say them. huge
weigh
record.
Time for a question. The video will stop. Which word means: weighs a lot?
Now some grammar: Comparatives. Add -er to short adjectives to compare two things.
Use ‘more’ with long adjectives. Use ‘than’ after them.
For example: A horse is faster than a cow.
For example: A parrot is more colourful than a crow.
Now listen, and read along. Animal records.
The blue whale is the biggest animal in the world.
It is longer than two buses and heavier than thirty elephants.
The cheetah is the fastest land animal. It can run faster than a car on a town road.
The bee hummingbird is one of the tiniest birds. It is smaller than your thumb!
Which animal do you think is more amazing?
Another question. The video will stop. What is the biggest animal in the world?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like heavy, fast, tiny.
You practised comparatives. And you read Animal records.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!
